Brief facts of the case is as follows :- The petitioner viz., N.Rajendran is the General Manager and the petitioner viz., N a v e e n J a i n i s t h e o c c u p i e r o f T i m e T e c h n o p l a s t L i m i t e d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.Nos. 7955 & 7958 of 2022 respectively situated at Gummidipoondi, which was started in the year of 2010 and it has got a compliment of 200 employees and eversince, it has commenced its operations, thereby it has been adhering in spirit in respect of all statutory compliances including safety and welfare of employees under the provisions of Factories Act.
texts.facts: However, the employee failed to take the first drum from the machine before completion of cycle time. He noticed that when the second drum parison ejection has started, he tried to pull out the missed first drum from the mould by placing his hand in top slide of blow machine, in which he was not supposed to rest his hand. Therefore, when the employee attempted to remove the drum by resting his hand in between the slide, the head slide came down and crushed his finger, which was not due to the fault of petitioner or its subordinates. Therefore, it would https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.Nos. 7955 & 7958 of 2022 contravene the provisions of Sec.41 Rule 61E and Sec.7A(1)(2) of Factories Act. Having not satisfied with their reply, immediately the respondent initiated complaint in order to prosecute the petitioners. However, as a factory manager and occupier, the petitioners were prosecuted by the respondent, thereby a complaint was lodged.
texts.arguments: If at all, any final order is passed with sufficient reason, it would enable the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.Nos. 7955 & 7958 of 2022 petitioner to prefer an appeal under Sec.107 of the Act.
